title: R’ Levi bar Perata or Palta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Chullin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.98a.9), Rav Shemen bar Abba cites Rav Idi bar Idi bar Gershom, who cites R’ Levi bar Perata in the name of R’ Nachum.

Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 10:6 brings the statement under the names “Ada bar Gershon, Rabbi Biri, Rabbi Levi bar Palta”; Hyman says it appears that it SHOULD READ Perata. Many of his homilies remain through R’ Yehudah son of R’ Simon, who reported them in his name: at the beginning of Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 3; Shemot Rabbah [supplied פמ״נח, unresolved]; Vayikra Rabbah 23:12; Bamidbar Rabbah 13:5; and Eichah Rabbah 1:34 and 1:38 [supplied פ״א־לד־לח].
Likewise R’ Yehudah son of R’ Soma (Hyman says it SHOULD READ Simon) reports in his name in Pesikta Rabbati, section “Vayehi HaMakriv.”
R’ Avin reports in his name in Shemot Rabbah 43:3.

notes.text: The corrupted Shemot Rabbah locator פמ״נח remains unresolved. Perata/Palta, Gershom/Gershon, Biri and Soma/Simon remain Hyman’s reported forms and corrections.

The whole saved Venice Terumot 10 scalar[5][7] has the unconnected sequence Zeira, Ada bar Gershon, full Rabbi Biriyy, full Rabbi Levi bar Palta, an elder, in Rabbi’s name. Hyman cites only part of it; no invented AND or intermediate reporting connector is added, and the omitted elder and Zeira are not imported into his body. Full Rabbi is supported locally for Biri and Levi bar Palta, not transferred to the heading or other citations. Hyman says IT APPEARS that Palta SHOULD READ Perata and independently that Soma SHOULD READ Simon. Gershom/Gershon, Perata/Palta and Soma/Simon remain. רפ״ג is beginning of chapter 3, not 83. פמ״נח remains unresolved; an inherited Bereshit 50:1 search snippet is not a newly inspected chapter or a resolved Shemot location. Eichah 34 and 38 remain a pair, with the supplied ambiguous separator preserved.

The consulted Chullin 98a has Gershom and Levi bar Perata, without a title before Levi. The Jerusalem Talmud has Gershon and Rabbi Levi bar Palta within a differently arranged chain. Shemot Rabbah 43:8 gives Yehudah bar Shalom in the name of Yehudah bar Simon in the name of Levi ben Perata. This identifies a corresponding passage for the unclear Shemot locator. The separate 43:3 passage has Avin in Levi bar Perata’s name. Bereshit Rabbah 50:1 gives Yehudah in the name of Simon in the name of Levi bar Perata. The consulted chapter 3 opening has Yehudah son of Simon in another attribution. Eikhah Rabbah 1:38 names Levi; the consulted 1:34 does not. Pesikta Rabbati 7, Vayehi HaMakriv, has Sima and Levi ben Perata. The parallel in Bamidbar Rabbah 13:5 has Simon and Levi ben Peratah.
